# Graft example: landing-page

This site is operated by editing files — there is no dashboard.
There are two equivalent interfaces: edit files directly, or use the MCP server.

## MCP server (preferred for agents)

`pnpm mcp` serves this site's content tools over stdio. It is already
registered in the repo-root `.mcp.json` as `graft-landing-page`:

    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "graft-landing-page": {
          "command": "pnpm",
          "args": ["--filter", "landing-page", "--silent", "mcp"]
        }
      }
    }

Tools:

- Content: `list_collections`, `describe_schema` (collections **and** functions),
  `list_content`, `get_content`, `search_content` (FTS; hits carry `sourcePath`),
  `write_content` (validate → write MDX → compile), `delete_content`
  (destructive, so ALWAYS human-gated: the first call files an approval and
  fails with its id; a human runs `graft approve <id>`; retry the same
  collection+slug with `approval: <id>` — one-shot, bound to that exact input),
  `explain_error`.
- Assets: `put_asset` — upload a binary and get the frontmatter reference.
  Local/stdio agents pass `path` (a file on this machine); remote agents pass
  `base64` + `key`. It refuses an existing key unless `overwrite: true` (the
  store keeps no version history). Equivalent to `graft asset put`.
- Functions: `list_functions`, `describe_function` (full args schema),
  `run_function` (same gates as `POST /api/fn/<name>`: access, audit, rate
  limits, human approval for destructive). You usually already have an
  identity: `graft mcp` acts as `GRAFT_DEV_TOKEN`, and over HTTP MCP the
  bearer you connected with is forwarded — only pass `authorization` to
  override it. Pass `approval` after `graft approve <id>`.
- Registry: `list_registry`, `describe_item` — browse owned primitives
  (blocks / fields / access rules / bundles) before installing one with
  `graft add <name>`. MCP shows what exists; the CLI installs it.

Every failure returns JSON with a `fix` — do what it says. Content writes land
as plain files under `content/`; commit them like any other change.

Remote agents (no stdio): the same tools are served over Streamable HTTP at
`POST /api/mcp` while the app is running (`pnpm dev`). Stateless, JSON
responses; set `GRAFT_MCP_REQUIRE_AUTH=1` to require a non-anonymous actor.
Generic projects can also run `graft mcp` (stdio) with DATABASE_URL.

## How to change content (by hand)

1. Edit or add MDX under `content/pages/`. Frontmatter must satisfy the
   `pages` collection in `graft.config.ts` (title: string; description:
   string — the meta description; tagline?: string; order?: number; slug:
   kebab-case, defaults to the filename).
   `order` is the nav position (ascending; home=1 — give a new page the next
   free number).
2. Run `pnpm compile` (the `graft compile` CLI). It validates every file and
   reports exactly what was added/changed/removed. Validation errors include a
   `fix` field — do what it says and re-run. `pnpm watch` (`graft dev`)
   recompiles on every save instead.
3. The running app (`pnpm dev`, http://localhost:3000) serves the new content
   on the next request. Home is the `home` slug; everything else is `/<slug>`.
4. Commit the change — git is the version history and the source of truth.

## How to add an image (or any binary)

1. Upload it: `pnpm exec graft asset put <file> [key]` (e.g.
   `graft asset put assets/hero.svg pages/home/hero.svg`), or the MCP
   `put_asset` tool (same rules; remote agents send `base64` + `key`). Uses
   the `S3_*` env from the repo-root `.env`; both print the frontmatter snippet.
2. Reference it from an `asset` field in frontmatter:

       image:
         key: pages/home/hero.svg
         alt: describe the image

3. `pnpm compile`. The app resolves the key to a URL at render time
   (presigned GET; set `S3_PUBLIC_URL` for stable public URLs).

## MDX bodies + blocks

Page bodies are **real MDX** (not markdown-only). Rendered by
`@graft/sdk-next` `MdxBody` with the generated map at
`components/mdx-components.ts`. Registry blocks land as PascalCase
components under `components/` and are auto-registered by `graft add`.

Example in content:

    <Callout type="info">Git is authoritative.</Callout>

    <Faq items={[{ question: "…", answer: "…" }]} />

Add more: `graft add callout`, `graft add faq`, `graft add seo`.

## Commerce (catalog + orders)

- Products: file-authoritative MDX under `content/products/` (see `/products`).
- Orders: db-authoritative via functions in `graft/commerce.ts`.
- `placeOrder` — public; `{ email, items: [{ productSlug, qty }] }`.
- `listOrders` / `updateOrderStatus` — need `commerce:orders:read` /
  `commerce:orders:write`.
- `cancelOrder` — destructive hard-delete; human-gated + write scope.

## Functions (typed server logic)

Functions are code in `graft.config.ts` + `graft/*` (`defineFunction`)
exported via `export const functions = { … }`, served while the app runs at:

    POST /api/fn/<name>        body: JSON object of the input fields
                               (empty body = {})

Success is `{ data: … }`; failure is GraftError JSON — `fix` says what to do,
`details.issues` lists field violations, and `explain_error` knows every code.

Registered functions (site + primitives):

- `pageStats` — query, no input; returns the live page slugs on the branch.
- `submitContact` — mutation, `public: true`; input `{ email, message? }`;
  stores a row in the `submissions` collection (the home-page contact form
  posts here). Rate-limited: 5/min per caller.
- `listSubmissions` — query, gated by `requireScopes("submissions:read")`;
  input `{ limit? }`; anonymous or unscoped callers get 401.
- `searchSubmissions` — query, same gate; input `{ query, limit? }`; full-text
  search over submissions, best match first.
- `deleteSubmission` — mutation, `destructive: true`; input `{ id }`; requires
  the `submissions:admin` scope AND human approval (see below).
- comments primitive: `postComment`, `listComments`, `moderateComment`, `deleteComment`.
- commerce primitive: `placeOrder`, `listOrders`, `updateOrderStatus`, `cancelOrder`.

To add a function: define input with the same `field.*` builders collections
use, write the handler against the standard context
(`{ input, db, actor, branch, request, correlationId }`), and add it to the
exported `functions` record. Mutations reject anonymous callers by default —
set `public: true` only when anonymous calls are the point (e.g. a form), or
supply an `access` rule (it replaces the default entirely). Mark anything
that deletes or irreversibly overwrites data `destructive: true`.

## Audit, rate limits, and human approval

Every function invocation writes an `audit_log` row (actor, correlationId,
git SHA, status, duration) — the `x-graft-correlation-id` response header is
the key into it.

Rate limits are per caller per function (your actor id; your IP when
anonymous). 429 responses carry `Retry-After`; every attempt counts, including
rejected ones, so back off — do not tight-loop retries.

Destructive functions never run directly. The workflow:

1. Call it normally → 403 `DESTRUCTIVE_OP_REQUIRES_APPROVAL` with
   `details.approvalId`. A pending approval (function + exact input) is filed.
2. A HUMAN reviews it: `pnpm exec graft approvals` lists pending ones;
   `graft approve <id>` or `graft deny <id>` decides. Agents must not run
   these themselves — ask the operator and wait.
3. Once approved, retry the EXACT same call carrying the approval id — over
   MCP pass it as the `approval` tool argument; over raw HTTP send the
   `x-graft-approval: <id>` header. Approvals are one-shot and bound to that
   exact input; any drift is `APPROVAL_INVALID` with the reason in details.

## Authentication (who is calling a function)

Callers are identified by `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, resolved by
`@graft/auth` (`app/api/fn/[name]/route.ts`). Two kinds of tokens work:

- **JWTs from this app's Better Auth instance** (`lib/auth.ts`, mounted at
  `/api/auth`). Sign in (`POST /api/auth/sign-in/email`), then mint a JWT at
  `GET /api/auth/token` — it carries submissions + commerce order scopes.
  The same verifier path accepts any trusted OIDC issuer (company IdP, Vercel
  Connect/Passport).
- **`GRAFT_DEV_TOKEN`** from the repo-root `.env` — a static local-dev
  credential; map scopes in the actor resolver for admin functions.


No header → anonymous. A bad/expired token is `TOKEN_INVALID` (401) with the
reason in `details` — fix the token; do not retry anonymously.

## Operational data (db-authoritative collections)

`submissions` has `authority: "db-authoritative"`: Postgres owns its rows and
the ONLY way in or out is through functions (`insertRecord` / `listRecords`
inside handlers — validated against the collection schema both directions).
Do not create `content/submissions/` files and do not use `write_content`
for it — both fail with AUTHORITY_MISMATCH and point you back here.

## Search

Full-text search is built in (Postgres, websearch syntax: plain words,
`"quoted phrases"`, `or`, `-exclusions`):

- **Content:** the `search_content` MCP tool, or `getGraft().searchContent(...)`
  from `lib/graft.ts` in server components. It searches the compiled index —
  results are as fresh as the last compile — and ranks slug matches over
  frontmatter over body. Hits carry a highlighted `snippet` and `sourcePath`.
- **Operational data:** per collection, through gated functions only
  (`searchRecords` inside a handler; `searchSubmissions` here).

## How to change the schema

Edit `graft.config.ts` (fields are built with `field.string()`,
`field.number({ optional: true })`, …), then update the MDX files to match and
run `pnpm compile`. Reads are typed from this file — no codegen step.

If the change breaks existing content or data (e.g. a new required field),
write a migration instead of hand-editing every file (see Migrations).

## Migrations (schema moved ahead of content/data)

Migrations are code: `migrations/<seq>-<name>.ts`, one per file, run in
filename order. The filename is the migration's identity in the
`migrations_applied` ledger — applied ones are skipped on re-runs.

- **Content migration** (file-authoritative collections):
  `export default defineContentMigration({ collection, description,
  transform })` from `@graft/content-migrations`. The transform gets each
  document's OLD `{ slug, data, body }` and returns the NEW `{ data, body? }`;
  output is validated against the current schema, files are rewritten in
  place, and the run compiles — the whole migration is a reviewable git
  commit. See `migrations/0001-pages-description.ts`.
- **Data migration** (db-authoritative collections):
  `export default defineDataMigration({ collection, description, transform })`
  from `@graft/core`. The transform maps each row's OLD `data` to the new
  shape; updates + ledger commit in ONE transaction. See
  `migrations/0002-submissions-email-lowercase.ts`.

Workflow: `pnpm migrate` (= `graft migrate`) is a DRY-RUN — it prints what
each pending migration would change and writes nothing. Execute with
`graft migrate --apply`, then commit the rewritten files. A failed run writes
nothing (all-or-nothing) and lists every failing file/row with the reason —
fix the transform and re-run. Compile errors after a schema change tell you
which files are missing what; that is the signal to write a content migration.

## Branches (preview a change without touching main)

A branch is an instant copy-on-write view. Two backends, same commands:
**overlay** (default) registers a row and scopes reads in the shared DB —
zero rows copied, reads fall through to the parent until the branch writes.
**neon** (`--backend neon`) forks a physically separate Postgres via the Neon
API (needs `NEON_API_KEY` + `GRAFT_NEON_PROJECT_ID` in .env). Either way:
content is inherited; **operational data (`data_records`) starts empty** —
previews inherit content, never operational data.

- `graft branch` — list branches (name, parent, backend).
- `graft branch create preview/my-change` — register a branch off main
  (`--from <parent>` to fork elsewhere; `--backend neon` for a physical
  fork). Then project into it with
  `graft compile --branch preview/my-change` — the CLI routes to the right
  database automatically; the app reads whichever branch its Graft client is
  configured for.
- `graft merge preview/my-change` — DRY-RUN by default, like `graft migrate`.
  It reports what `--apply` would do: replay migrations the branch applied but
  main hasn't (data migrations run for real; content migrations just get a
  ledger row — their file rewrites arrive via the git merge), move the
  branch's `data_records` rows onto the target, and recompile the working
  tree into the target. **git-merge the branch's commits first** — content is
  git-authoritative, so `graft merge` compiles whatever tree you run it from.
- `graft branch drop preview/my-change` — overlay: unregister and purge the
  branch's content/data/ledger rows (audit history stays); neon: delete the
  fork and its endpoint.

## Caching & revalidation (optional; reads are force-dynamic today)

This app renders `dynamic = "force-dynamic"`, so every request sees the latest
compile — no cache, no revalidation needed. Graft ships the cache-tag contract
for when you want cached/ISR rendering instead:

- **Tag reads** with Next 16 `'use cache'` + `cacheTag`, using the helpers from
  `@graft/sdk-next` (re-exported from sdk-core):
  ```ts
  import { cacheTag, cacheLife } from "next/cache";
  import { documentTag } from "@graft/sdk-next";
  async function getPage(slug: string) {
    "use cache";
    cacheTag(documentTag("main", "pages", slug)); // list reads: collectionTag(...)
    cacheLife("max");
    return getGraft().getContent("pages", slug);
  }
  ```
  (`'use cache'` needs `cacheComponents: true` in next.config.ts.)
- **Invalidate after a compile** by POSTing the compile's ChangeSet to
  `POST /api/revalidate` (`{ branch, changes }`, bearer-gated) — it calls
  `revalidateContent(branch, changes)`, which fires `revalidateTag` for only
  the per-doc + per-collection tags that changed. Inside a Server Action, use
  `updateContent(branch, changes)` instead for read-your-own-writes.

The contract is precise: an unchanged-only compile revalidates nothing (the
hash-diff `ChangeSet` is the invalidation input), and tags are branch-scoped so
a preview never busts main's cache.

## Layout of this app

- `graft.config.ts` — collections (the schema; single source of truth)
- `content/pages/*.mdx` — the authored documents
- `migrations/*.ts` — content/data migrations (`pnpm migrate` to inspect)
- `lib/graft.ts` — the typed read client (`getContent`, `listContent`,
  `searchContent`)
- `app/page.tsx`, `app/[slug]/page.tsx` — routes that render documents
- `app/api/revalidate/route.ts` — the cache-revalidation webhook (POST a ChangeSet)
- `pnpm compile` / `pnpm watch` — project content into Postgres (the `graft` CLI)

## Rules

- Never write to the database directly; it is a derived index. Files win.
- Slugs are kebab-case (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens).
- `DATABASE_URL` comes from the repo-root `.env`.

## scoped-access (primitive)

`graft/scoped-access.ts` names your token scopes and exposes access rules.

- `requireModerator` gates a function so only callers whose token carries the
  `content:moderate` scope may run it (anonymous/unscoped → 401 UNAUTHORIZED).
- Edit the `SCOPES` map to match what your token issuer emits, then reuse the
  rules on any function's `access:`.
- Requires `@graft/auth` in the project (mint/verify tokens there).

## comments (primitive)

Moderated comments backed by db-authoritative rows (`graft/comments.ts`).
Functions are served at POST /api/fn/<name>:

- `postComment` — public; `{ pageSlug, author, body }` → stores it unapproved. 5/min per caller.
- `listComments` — public; `{ pageSlug, limit? }` → approved comments, newest first.
- `moderateComment` — `{ id, approved }` → approve/hide. Needs the `content:moderate` scope.
- `deleteComment` — `{ id }` → destructive: files an approval (`graft approve <id>`), then
  retry with the approval id (MCP: the `approval` argument; HTTP: the
  `x-graft-approval` header); also needs `content:moderate`.

New comments are hidden until `moderateComment` approves them. Depends on the
`scoped-access` primitive (`graft/scoped-access.ts`) for the moderation gate.
